content.text: {"relation":"DIVERGENT","consensus_summary":"The Gospel is the good news of salvation accomplished through Jesus Christ's life, death, and resurrection — God's saving reign inaugurated in Christ, received by faith — anchored above all in 1 Corinthians 15:1-4, Romans 1:16, and Mark 1:14-15, with the kingdom announcement, the four written Gospels, and law/gospel or social readings as complementary emphases rather than rival cores.","book_summary":"The Gospel is the gospel of the kingdom, identified specifically as the renewed covenant and the law going forth from Zion (Isa 2:3; Jer 31:33) — a message that was also preached to Israel in the wilderness (Heb 4:2) — explicitly set against the commonly taught view that the gospel is the news that Christ died for our sins, was buried, and rose again.","consensus_core_identification":"Gospel = the proclamation of God's saving act in Jesus Christ, centered on his death for sins and resurrection (with the arrival of God's kingdom in him).","book_core_identification":"Gospel = the announcement of the renewed covenant — Torah written on hearts and the law going forth from Zion — i.e., kingdom-covenant instruction, not (primarily) the death-burial-resurrection message.","core_relation":"CONTRADICTS","extension_relation":"PARTIAL_RECLASSIFICATION","boundary_disagreement":"The book admits gospel proclamations that the consensus core excludes — notably the message preached to the wilderness generation before Christ (Heb 4:2) and the eschatological law-from-Zion proclamation (Isa 2:3) — while demoting the 1 Corinthians 15 death-and-resurrection content from the gospel's defining center to a 'commonly taught' view it sets itself against.","material_contradiction":"The consensus identifies the gospel's content as the Christ-event itself (Christ died, was buried, rose again — 1 Cor 15:1-4); the book's own common-view note flags exactly that identification as the view it departs from, replacing the content with the renewed covenant and Torah from Zion. Both cannot be the defining content of 'the gospel' in the same sense: if the gospel is essentially covenant-law instruction preached even to pre-Christ Israel, it is not essentially the announcement of Christ's death and resurrection.","rationale":"Although 'gospel of the kingdom' appears in the consensus as a common alternative emphasis, that alternative still centers God's reign arriving through Jesus, with the Christ-event integral. The book goes further: it defines the gospel as the renewed covenant and the law going forth from Zion, and its common-view note explicitly brackets the death-resurrection identification as the position it replaces. Hebrews 4:2 is deployed to show the gospel predates and is independent of the Christ-event, which no consensus reading (including the kingdom alternative) holds as the core. This is replacement of the central identification, not mere boundary refinement, even though extensions overlap (both still call the kingdom announcement 'gospel').","citation_support":"PARTIAL","strongest_objection":"The 'gospel of the kingdom' is listed as a common consensus alternative (Mark 1:14-15; Matt 4:23), and Isaiah 52:7 ('Thy God reigneth') is shared background in both readings; one could therefore argue the book merely refines that recognized kingdom-gospel alternative by specifying its content as covenant and Torah, making REFINED the better verdict. Additionally, Response A's dispensationalist minority alternative already distinguishes a 'gospel of the kingdom' from the Pauline gospel, partially anticipating the book's move.","confidence":"medium"}
